rationales: Butter is classified as a liquid dispersed in a solid.
Fog is liquid droplets dispersed in a gas.
Salt in water is a solid dissolved in a liquid.
Sugar in water is a solid dissolved in a liquid.
A triple bond contains three shared pairs, or six electrons.
Eight electrons would represent four shared pairs, not a triple bond.
Four electrons represent two shared pairs, which form a double bond.
Three electrons do not make a triple covalent bond; each shared pair contains two electrons.
Covalent bonding generally involves sharing electrons rather than their transfer.
Polar covalent bonding involves unequal sharing between nonmetals.
An electropositive element transfers electrons to an electronegative element, forming an ionic bond.
Coordinate covalent bonding occurs when one atom supplies both electrons in a shared pair.
HCl is diatomic, with two atoms per molecule.
CH₄ has five atoms per molecule, so it is polyatomic.
H₂ is diatomic, with two atoms per molecule.
CO₂ is triatomic, with three atoms per molecule.
HCl is a covalent compound represented by molecules.
C₆H₆ is a covalent compound represented by molecules.
NaCl is an ionic compound represented by formula units.
H₂O is a covalent compound represented by molecules.
98 g is not the mass of one H₂SO₄ molecule; the corresponding molar mass is 98 g/mol.
One H₂SO₄ molecule has a molecular mass of 98 amu.
9.8 amu is too small; the molecular mass is 98 amu.
9.8 g is not the mass of one molecule or its molar mass.
An anion forms by gaining electrons, not removing them.
Removing electrons from an atom does not produce a molecule.
An atom that loses electrons becomes a positively charged cation.
A molecular ion is a charged group of bonded atoms, not the usual product of electron removal from one atom.
Light water is ordinary water containing mostly protium.
Soft water has low concentrations of calcium and magnesium ions.
Hard water contains dissolved calcium or magnesium salts.
Deuterium is used to make heavy water, D₂O.
Lattice energy is associated with forming an ionic solid from gaseous ions.
Ionization energy is the energy required to remove an electron.
Electronegativity describes an atom’s attraction for shared electrons in a bond.
Electron affinity is the energy released when an atom gains an electron.
Each oxygen atom in O₂ completes its octet by sharing electrons.
BF₃ is electron deficient because boron has only six electrons around it.
Each nitrogen atom in N₂ completes its octet through a triple bond.
Nitrogen in NH₃ has an octet, including its lone pair.
Grams of solute per 100 g of solution express mass-by-mass percentage.
Mass-by-volume percentage uses grams of solute per 100 mL of solution.
Volume-by-mass percentage uses volume of solute per mass of solution.
Volume-by-volume percentage uses volumes of solute and solution.
Benzene is nonpolar and generally dissolves nonpolar substances.
Ether is less suitable than water for dissolving polar covalent compounds in this classification.
Water is polar and dissolves many polar covalent compounds.
Petrol is nonpolar and generally dissolves nonpolar substances.
Coordinate covalent bonding involves a shared pair donated by one atom, not electron transfer.
Covalent bonding forms by sharing electrons between atoms.
Metallic bonding involves delocalized electrons among metal atoms.
Electron transfer between atoms forms an ionic bond.
Groups are the vertical columns of the periodic table.
Blocks are regions based on the type of subshell being filled.
Periods are the horizontal rows of the periodic table.
Triads are groups of three elements, not the horizontal lines in the long-form table.
HCl and H₂O both contain polar covalent bonds.
C₂H₂ has nonpolar C–H bonds in this classification, although H₂O has polar bonds.
N₂ has a nonpolar bond, although H₂O has polar bonds.
Cl₂ and O₂ each have nonpolar bonds between identical atoms.
